newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Extracts from RBNZ pamphlet for exporters.
newsitem.headline: Extracts from RBNZ pamphlet for exporters.

text.p: Following are extracts from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's pamphlet entitled: "The impact of monetary policy on exporters", published on Friday.

* The Reserve Bank acknowledges that recently the economic climate has been very tough for exporters, and that, in part, this has been due to tight monetary conditions required to control inflationary pressures... However, when inflationary pressures are strong, as in the last two years, loosening monetary policy to assist exporters would be a hollow gesture.

An initial fall in the exchange rate would give exporters temporary respite, but it would be short lived. The flow-on effect of such an easing would be higher inflation, rapidly driving up exporters' input costs. Any advantage from looser monetary conditions would be ephemeral, while in the long term exporters would have to carry the negative effects of inflation, like everyone else.
